top_3_developments.headline: US and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury with strikes on Iranian nuclear, military, and leadership targets; Iran retaliated with missile strikes on Israel and US bases
top_3_developments.summary: The US and Israel conducted joint pre-dawn strikes on February 28, 2026, targeting Iran's nuclear program, missile sites, naval assets, IRGC facilities, and leadership including Supreme Leader Khamenei, whose status reports as presumed dead or uncertain. Iran responded by firing approximately 40 missiles at Israel and attacking US bases across Bahrain, Kuwait, UAE, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Iraq, with most intercepted but some impacts reported. Operations continue as an open-ended campaign aimed at regime change, prompting FBI nationwide alerts and congressional debate on war powers.
top_3_developments.source: Fox News live updates, Institute for the Study of War

top_3_developments.headline: DOJ released over 3.5 million pages of Epstein files, including 2,000 unreleased videos, with latest batch on January 30, 2026
top_3_developments.summary: The DOJ published more than 3.5 million pages under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, exceeding the December 2025 deadline, featuring photos, videos, court records, and documents mentioning figures like Trump, Clinton, and Musk without established wrongdoing. Heavy redactions protect 14 investigative targets and victims; London police launched a probe into a former UK minister on February 4. Disclosures remain ongoing with significant new footage.

top_3_developments.headline: US-Ukrainian delegations met in Geneva on February 26 amid stalled Russia-Ukraine talks over Donbas
top_3_developments.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Rustem Umerov and US officials including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner synchronized positions in Geneva on economic support packages ahead of March trilateral talks. Russia conducted major strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure but signaled no urgency for a deal, insisting on full Donbas control without Ukrainian security guarantees. No direct Russia-Ukraine talks occurred on February 28.

signal_status.headline: US and Israel conducting ongoing strike campaign against Iran under Operation Epic Fury; Iran retaliating with missile strikes on Israel and US bases.
signal_status.summary: The US and Israel launched major strikes on Iran on February 28, 2026, targeting nuclear and missile programs, naval assets, military sites, and leadership including attempts on Supreme Leader Khamenei, with his status uncertain.[1][2] Iran has responded by firing approximately 35 missiles at Israel and attacking 14 US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, UAE, Jordan, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.[1][2] Operations continue with no set end date, involving close US-Israeli coordination aimed at regime change.[1][2]
sources: Institute for the Study of War (understandingwar.org)

signal_status.headline: Board of Peace held inaugural meeting on Feb 19, 2026, pledging $7B for Gaza reconstruction; additional board members to be announced soon.
signal_status.summary: The Board of Peace, chaired by President Trump, conducted its first meeting on February 19, 2026, in Washington DC at the Donald J. Trump United States Institute of Peace, where members pledged $7 billion for Gaza reconstruction, peacekeeping troops, and investment as part of Phase Two of the Gaza ceasefire plan.[1][3] Yesterday, the White House announced the formation of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), aligning with UNSCR 2803, with further Executive Board members expected in coming weeks.[2] Criticisms persist regarding vagueness, underfunding, and Hamas disarmament issues, but no new meetings or major actions reported since Feb 19.[3]
sources: Arab Center DC on inaugural meeting and pledges[1]
White House statement on NCAG formation[2]
Al Jazeera on Feb 19 meeting details[3]

signal_status.headline: Gulf SWFs sustaining high deployment levels into 2026 with major US tech investments and regional restructuring.
signal_status.summary: Gulf sovereign wealth funds, led by Saudi PIF and UAE's Mubadala, deployed $119 billion in 2025, capturing 43% of global sovereign activity, with continued momentum into 2026 including PIF's involvement in a $108 billion bid for Warner Bros. Discovery and Abu Dhabi's launch of the restructured L’IMAD fund in January 2026.[1][2][4] No new deals are reported in February 2026, but expectations persist for strong M&A and exits driven by PIF, alongside ongoing portfolio reviews by QIA.[3][4] Inward capital flows reached 9.6% of regional GDP in 2025, supporting further outbound investments despite lower oil prices.[5]
sources: CAIA February 2026 report on Gulf SWF activity[1]
A&O Shearman on Middle East M&A and SWFs[3]
BNP Paribas on GCC capital flows[5]

signal_status.headline: DOJ Epstein Files Transparency Act releases exceed 3.5 million pages; ongoing document disclosure with latest materials published January 30, 2026
signal_status.summary: The Department of Justice has published over 3.5 million pages in compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, significantly exceeding the original December 19, 2025 deadline. The release includes tens of thousands of pages of photos, videos, court records, FBI and DOJ documents, and emails, with approximately 2,000 videos containing previously unreleased footage. The disclosure process remains active with continued revelations including mentions of prominent figures and investigations into individuals connected to Epstein's operations.

signal_status.headline: US-Ukrainian talks in Geneva on February 26 ongoing amid stalled Russia-Ukraine negotiations over Donbas; Russia signals no rush for deal.
signal_status.summary: On February 26, 2026, Ukrainian and US delegations met in Geneva, led by Rustem Umerov and Steve Witkoff with Jared Kushner, to synchronize positions ahead of trilateral talks in early March, focusing on economic support and prosperity packages for Ukraine. Russia launched a massive missile and drone strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure hours before the meeting but showed no direct involvement; Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov and Kremlin spokesman Peskov stated there are no deadlines and it's too premature for forecasts on a deal. Negotiations remain deadlocked over Russia's demand for full control of Donbas, which Ukraine rejects without security guarantees; no Russia-Ukraine direct talks confirmed on February 28.
